title: Fort Jesus, Mombasa
summary: Fort Jesus stands on a coral-rock spur at the southern edge of Mombasa Old Town, Kenya. The Portuguese built it in 1593–96 to designs by the Italian military architect Giovanni Battista Cairati, with four bastions around a central courtyard. The Omani Arabs drove the Portuguese out in 1696, and from 1895 to 1958 the fort served as a prison.

uncertainty.note: Start is the beginning of the Portuguese building in 1593, completed in 1596 (ICOMOS: erected in 1593-96). End is the present: the fort stands as a protected property.

phases.description: Built by the Portuguese in 1593-96, completed three years after work began (ICOMOS).
After a revolt, curtain walls were built on the landward side, new walls added on three bastions, and an elliptical bastion and second gate added at the main gate (ICOMOS).
The Omani Arabs besieged the fort and drove out the Portuguese; further modifications repaired and reinforced the damaged fort (ICOMOS).
Converted to a prison under British rule, with a kitchen and a gallows among the added buildings (ICOMOS).
Designated a National Park in 1958 to protect the fort and a 100 m strip round it; protected today under the National Museums and Heritage Act 2006 (ICOMOS).
